outcomes: A serverless or short-lived workload exports its telemetry by pushing it, without needing to be scraped
An unreachable or failing collector degrades observability and nothing else
A container that exits promptly still delivers its last batch of measurements
A request's span is attributed to the right service and joined to the caller's trace
nonGoals: Running a collector, or defining collector-side retention, sampling, or routing
Exporting via gRPC OTLP or via an OpenTelemetry exporter SDK; the wire is rendered directly as OTLP/JSON over HTTP
Exporting logs implicitly: the log sink is attached to the application logger deliberately
Promising strict compatibility between every pre-1.0 minor release

requirements.text: Configuring an OTLP endpoint wires a periodic metric reader and a span exporter that POST OTLP/JSON to the collector's metrics and traces paths, and an explicitly supplied reader or exporter is never replaced by that auto-wiring.
An OTLP configuration with an empty endpoint fails at configure rather than starting a workload whose telemetry silently goes nowhere.
Collector errors are dropped rather than propagated, and the log sink batches records onto a background flush, so neither export failures nor collector latency reach the request path.
The metric reader flushes periodically and once more during provider shutdown, so a short-lived container does not drop its last batch.
Shutdown bounds the flush by the configured shutdown timeout and reports tracer and meter shutdown failures together rather than stopping at the first one.
A configured service name or version is merged onto the SDK's default resource so telemetry SDK attributes are preserved, and leaving both unset leaves the providers' own default resource untouched.
An unset sample rate samples every trace, while an explicit rate of zero samples none, so "not configured" and "deliberately disabled" stay distinguishable.

The HTTP middleware ends its span for every outcome: a nil response, a server-error response marked errored, and a downstream panic that is recorded on the span and then re-raised so an outer recovery middleware still behaves normally.
An inbound W3C traceparent header is extracted so the request's span continues the caller's trace instead of starting an unrelated one.
Request durations shorter than a millisecond are recorded with their real value rather than truncated to zero.

The generated-client bridge counts every stored answer a generated client returns after its provider call failed as rpc.client.cache.stale_served, on the same rpc.system, rpc.service, rpc.method and network.protocol.name attributes as the call metrics, and never as an attribute carrying the answer's age.

Reading the plugin's provider registrations has no side effect, configure installs the global providers exactly once per application lifetime, the plugin rebuilds cleanly after a stop, and the error-count bridge hook is removed on stop.
